title: Add NVTX ranges, runtime counters, microbench harness, and perf dashboard for runtime profiling
author: Ava Chen
description: This PR adds low-overhead NVTX ranges and runtime counters across key runtime hot paths (kernel launch, attention, KV cache ops, and continuous batching scheduler), a microbenchmark harness for isolated measurement, and a Grafana perf dashboard + CI perf check to make regressions observable. Motivation: we frequently lack consistent instrumentation for cross-stack perf investigations (ENG-1723). This work provides: 1) NVTX ranges around attention kernels, kv cache GET/PUT, kv-cache hit/miss paths, batch formation and scheduling, and response assembly; 2) lightweight atomic counters exposed via /metrics for counts like kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_misses, batch_size_histogram, kernel_launch_ns_total; 3) a microbench harness under tools/perf/microbenchmarks that can run targeted scenarios (attention-only, kv-cache-only, continuous-batch latency/throughput) and emit structured CSV artifacts for CI; 4) a Grafana dashboard (docs and json) with prebuilt panels for end-to-end latency breakdown, kernel time, kv-cache hit ratio, and batching efficiency; 5) a CI perf-check job that runs microbench nightly and fails on regressions beyond thresholds. Checklist: ensure NVTX calls are guarded with compile flag; verify atomic counters have minimal contention; add unit/test wrappers for microbench; update docs with dashboard links; add release notes. This description bundles motivation, changes, and verification steps for reviewers.
